records.subagent_summary: My 8 rollouts scored 1/8 (exec 149.338). Every failure judged ignorance by counting pairs consistent with the public number itself, then said the holder can just subtract or divide, wrote contradiction/impossible (17-54 times in the loopers), and finished on looks: 143 boxed three times, 13 once justified explicitly by primality, one pair endorsed for being non-prime. Three burned the 16384-token cap on that loop. Not one rollout pooled the partners a single private value admits across BOTH unstated readings, so none ever saw where residual ambiguity lives, and none allowed the two values to be equal. The incumbent says predicate abstractly and the model echoes the word without executing it, so the revision makes the pooled per-value count the one operation, states that pinning under a single choice is not a contradiction, replaces guessing with an intersect-the-survivors termination rule, and names the two aesthetic tie-breakers actually observed as banned.

records.mutation: extend-nth-root-rule-to-absorbing-c-into-the-power, plus attribution rule replacing the bare no-enumeration ban
records.subagent_summary: All 8 rollouts correct (3.5k-10.2k tokens, 3-42 hedges), so training is saturated and the lever is transfer plus wasted budget. Every rollout had the locus within its first ~2k characters, then enumerated roots anyway (10-66 branch expressions each) despite the incumbent stop rule. The instructive one (10.2k tokens, 42 hedges) absorbed the constant into the power, writing c(z-b)^n as (cz)^n without nth-rooting c, so its branch solved to a point that failed its own modulus ratio; it then spent ~6k tokens doubting the modulus law itself before recovering. Two more re-litigated necessary-vs-sufficient and one manufactured a rival constant-|z| circle from a bad rearrangement. Diagnosis: the k rule covers only the explicit nth root, not the equivalent absorb-into-the-power move, and a bare enumeration ban leaves a contradiction unattributed. So the revision extends the nth-root rule to absorption and adds an attribution rule: a violating candidate indicts the algebra, not the law.

5/8 correct; all three failures died at the 16384 cap. Two never built the edge frame: they placed the covering square by offsetting the shared point a full side or half-diagonal in BOTH directions (-0.5..1.5, -1.5..2.5), which makes that point interior, so the small square looked wholly covered, overlap 1, and one committed that value. The third did compute the correct clipped area and union early (~3.9k chars), then reopened the angle question and burned ~50k chars on rotated-square algebra (112 rotation mentions) without closing. Winners reached the same first value and closed fast. The incumbent only forbids extending a full side both ways, and a bare ban loses to a concrete-looking offset; its rotation clause stayed conditional and unused. So the frame becomes constructive (list the cover's vertices as P plus non-negative multiples of its two edge directions, a negative coefficient being a self-check failure) and the closure becomes an executable congruence argument.

4/8 with the incumbent; 3 of the 4 failures truncated at the token cap after already deriving N x d. Each stalled the same way: it called the product 'too high / seems too large', reopened tightness, argued a function's own consecutive values would have to step by the common difference and so 'must be linear', then oscillated (one drifted from the product down to d and boxed that). None ever performed the incumbent's P = T + c*prod(x-n_j) check concretely; they debated it instead. The fourth failure stopped normally, never grouped at all: it labelled a polynomial per term, chained adjacent board entries, and answered N. So the live faults are doubt about a legitimately large product and an uncertified construction, not aggregation. This revision keeps the proven skeleton, states affirmatively that exceeding N is expected, and converts tightness into a single terminating substitution check rather than a claim to be re-litigated.

7/8 correct (149.342). The lone failure is deterministic and identical across recent rounds: it fits the parameters, finds the right t, rejects the degenerate root, then evaluates the new height by rewriting an argument below 1 as a power of the base's reciprocal and copying that exponent, producing a negative height where the correct one is positive. Both new vertices inherit the flipped sign, so the cross product is computed on a reflected pair and the area is wrong. Critically, the rollout DID substitute back to check, but re-ran the same inverse conversion, so the check was circular and confirmed the error. The incumbent's 'take each new height from f' is precisely the step that fails. The revision therefore demands a forward, non-circular test (does base^y reproduce the argument) and states the resulting sign rule, while compressing the pipeline into a portable form.

1/8 (idx 1, and it wavered between 1/16 and 1/8 before committing). Three failure clusters. (i) Uniformity re-imported for the graded part: idx 0 gave 1/24 then 1/4 from each bag equally likely to move last; idx 3 said each element has equal chance of any position. (ii) Template exponents guessed with no walk of the moves: 1/2^(n-1), 1/2^n, 1/2^(2n-1) produced 1/8, 1/16, 1/128 on part a. (iii) Undercounting the run: idx 4,5,7 priced the graded event using only the target's own two carries (1/4) or a lone 1/2, ignoring the choices needed to clear the items above it. Idx 2,3,6 hit the token cap oscillating between rival formulas. So the incumbent states arrival-rank and bans 1/n, yet the pricing step is guessed rather than executed. This revision makes freeness operational (free exactly when both piles can be drawn from, so track pile sizes while walking the word), says clearing choices count too, and bans template exponents in favour of hand-walking the smallest instance.

All 8 rollouts scored 0. Each built the n=2 and n=3 toy, but only 3 reached n=4+, and 5 abandoned numbers midway to expand (x-1)...(x-2004) at full size, chase its x-coefficient, or introduce harmonic sums H_n (40-100 mentions of 2004! or H_n each). 5 hit the 16384-token cap without answering. The 3 that finished guessed a law from only two cases and shipped 1/2005, 1/6, 1/2004 -- no back-substitution, no ratio comparison, and one even declared even/odd cases exceptional. The incumbent already bans symbolic general-size algebra, but the model does not recognize the long-product / harmonic-sum expansion as an instance of that ban. So I name those three concrete detours as an explicit tripwire with an order to drop the line and return to numeric cases, and I keep the ratio-of-consecutive-answers law, the fixed toy count-match, and back-substitution.

7/8 rollouts correct; the single failure (and the longest, 15.5k tokens) is not arithmetic. Every rollout derived the divisor set from integrality correctly, then stalled on a tie between the maximum candidate and a much smaller one equal to the group count, spending 40 backtracks re-arguing whether each group could hold exactly one unit. The loser resolved it by narrative plausibility ("most reasonable interpretation"), picked the group-count candidate and lost; winners reached the maximum but only via weak ad-hoc appeals, so the tie-break is luck. The incumbent already says a group count is never N by itself, but rollouts evade that by asserting units-per-group = 1, which is formally consistent. So I named that specific escape hatch: the per-group factor is a separate unknown that must not be silently set to 1, and ties are never broken by which story sounds plausible. Kept the divisor/gcd and bounded-window branches intact since removing them cost train in rounds 1-2.

7/8 correct (3.4k-5.3k tokens). The one failure burned the full 16384-token cap: centering correctly, it then substituted p(x)-r=A(x-r)^n twice, writing q(p(x))=r+B[A^3(x-r)^3]^3, so it got BA^9 and concluded B^2=A^8, B=+-A^4 (8 mentions). Both branches gave high-degree equations in the center; it trial-substituted integer centers for most of its output and only stumbled onto a consistent center too late to finish. Correct rollouts all reached A^3=B^3 in their first page. Rounds 9/10 (exponent audits), 14/15 (factoring rules) and 16 (no-ratio) all lost heldout, so instead of another audit this revision adds a portable validation rule: any necessary condition must hold for a solution family you already know (here p=q), which flags the mis-nesting in one line and transfers to any functional equation.

2/8 correct with the incumbent. Three of six failures boxed 2 by the same argument: each sub-step is a self-inverse block swap, therefore the composite is a product of transpositions of order 2. The incumbent's 'nested ranges never compose to disjoint swaps' clause states the conclusion but gives no test, so rollouts overrode it with the plausible involution/lcm-of-2s claim and never traced a state. One boxed a linear formula after inventing cycle lists (a 6-cycle for one size, an 8-cycle for the next) it never traced. Two hit the token cap thrashing over whether the composed map or its inverse was right after a small-size trace. So the revision replaces the assertion with a checkable reason (involutions compose to order 2 only when they commute, and overlapping ranges do not), bans uncited cycle lengths, and turns vague minimality into a concrete certificate: show m returns and m/p does not for each prime p dividing m.
